title: The Voyage of the Argonauts
text:
In the epic by Apollonius of Rhodes, Jason was sent by his uncle, King Pelias, to fetch the Golden Fleece from Colchis, at the far eastern end of the Black Sea. He could not do it alone, so he gathered the greatest heroes of Greece to sail with him on the Argo, a ship built by Argus with the help of the goddess Athena.

The crew was chosen for its gifts as much as its courage. Tiphys was the helmsman. Lynceus could see farther than any other man. Orpheus played music that calmed the sea and set the rowers' rhythm. Zetes and Calais, the winged sons of the North Wind, chased off the Harpies who were tormenting the blind prophet Phineus. Polydeuces, the boxer, beat a brutal king who challenged every stranger to a fight.

In return Phineus told them how to pass the Clashing Rocks: release a dove first, and if it got through, row with everything they had. They did, and the Argo made it through, losing only the tip of its stern. Even the strongest of them, Heracles, was left behind early on, when he went searching for his lost companion Hylas and the ship sailed without him. The voyage went on without its greatest fighter, carried by everyone else.
lesson: A strong crew is built from different gifts, each used at the right moment. No single star, however strong, is indispensable if the rest of the team works as one.
people: Jason, Tiphys, Lynceus, Orpheus, Zetes, Calais, Polydeuces, Heracles, Phineus
location: Alexandria (Egypt); voyage from Greece to Colchis (modern Georgia)
source: Apollonius of Rhodes, Argonautica, Books 1 and 2
